title: Environment Variables & Configuration
description: Manage API keys and settings with environment variables in Vite.

slides.title: Why Environment Variables?
slides.content:
# Keep Secrets Out of Source Code

Environment variables allow you to configure your app differently depending on the environment (development, staging, production). Common uses:

- API base URLs
- API keys (only for client‑side, but still better to separate)
- Feature flags

Vite uses `.env` files and exposes variables prefixed with `VITE_` to the client.

slides.title: Using .env Files
slides.content:
# Create `.env` and `.env.production`

```bash
# .env (loaded in all environments)
VITE_API_URL=https://api.dev.example.com

# .env.production (loaded only in production)
VITE_API_URL=https://api.example.com
```

In your code, access them via `import.meta.env`:
```javascript
const apiUrl = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL
```

Vite also provides built‑in variables: `import.meta.env.MODE`, `import.meta.env.PROD`, `import.meta.env.DEV`.

slides.title: Example: Dynamic API Base URL

quizData.question: How do you access a custom environment variable in a Vite‑powered Vue app?
quizData.explanation: Vite exposes environment variables on `import.meta.env`, and only variables prefixed with `VITE_` are exposed to the client.
